messages:
nina: quick update from the Argo-11B quant probe (INT5/INT8/fp16) on the onboarding slices. dropping a compact handoff for product + runtime.
oscar: nice, TL;DR?
mei: also add unit cost numbers pls.
nina: TL;DR: INT5 pushes biggest savings but shows a localized regression on multi-step instruction and code synthesis. INT8 is safe for most slices; fp16 still best for long-document fidelity.
raj: metrics please.
nina: measured on GTN-sample (5k requests): cost per 1k tokens -> fp16 $0.98, INT8 $0.47, INT5 $0.29. Delta macro-F1 vs fp16 -> INT8 -0.5pt, INT5 -2.9pt. Hallucination probe (800 examples): INT8 +0.6% abs, INT5 +2.2% abs.
oscar: latency impacts?
nina: p95 latency: fp16 195ms baseline, INT8 206ms (+11ms), INT5 248ms (+53ms) due to extra KV reconstruction on our INT5 fallback path.
mei: what about prefix cache hit-rate?
nina: kvcache hits: fp16 66%, INT8 65%, INT5 59% 1% drop vs fp16 for INT5. runtime-bug suspected: INT5 KV chunking truncates delimiters.
runtime-bot: nightly-smoke: pass. quant-kernel-errors: 0. kvcache-regression-score INT5=0.72 INT8=0.08.
raj: we asked for a single product metric earlier. I made "Beacon" = 0.6*QualityNorm + 0.25*CostSavingNorm + 0.15*(1/LatencyNorm) where higher is better and cost savings & latency mapped so bigger is better.
oscar: paste normalized snapshot pls.
nina: snapshot:
```
Variant | QualityNorm | CostSavingNorm | InvLatencyNorm | Beacon
fp16    | 1.00        | 0.00           | 1.00           | 1.00
INT8    | 0.995       | 0.488          | 0.943          | 0.995*0.6 + 0.488*0.25 + 0.943*0.15 = 0.90
INT5    | 0.971       | 0.704          | 0.786          | = 0.86
```
(note: CostSavingNorm scaled so INT5 highest; InvLatencyNorm = baseline_latency / variant_latency)
mei: Beacon prefers INT8 for GTN slices 1 good. product will push for a clear default + exceptions list.
nina: recommendation: default -> INT8 for GTN onboarding. Exceptions -> route to fp16 for long-doc (>3k tokens), contract/legal, and multi-step code generation tasks detected by signal. INT5 -> keep shadowed at 8% to collect slice-level failures and opt-in only for low-risk batch pipelines.
raj: routing snippet for runtime team?
nina: use rule: `if (metadata.task=="code_multi_step" || metadata.slice in ["legal","contracts"] || metadata.context_tokens>3000) model=\"fp16\" elif metadata.traffic_profile==\"bulk_low_risk\" model=\"INT5\" else model=\"INT8\"`
oscar: ops plan: 5% canary for INT8 default (swap from fp16), shadow INT5 @8%, ramp INT8 to 40% after 72h if no regression signals.
runtime-bot: canary flag created `feature.gtn.argo11b.quant_canary=0.05`. shadow config: infra://gtn/argo11b/shadow-int5.json
mei: product blurb for onboarding doc (2 lines): "Recommend INT8 as the default for Argo-11B in GTN beta 1 it balances cost and fidelity. Route long-docs, contracts, and multi-step code tasks to fp16. INT5 is shadow-only pending KV-chunk kernel fix."
oscar: concise scorecard line for playbook: [Variant, CostPer1k, DeltaF1, p95_ms] -> INT8, $0.47, -0.5pt, +11ms; INT5, $0.29, -2.9pt, +53ms; fp16, $0.98, 0pt, baseline.
raj: followups: 1) runtime ticket to debug INT5 KV-chunk truncation (assign runtime team) 2) PR to gtn/docs with blurb + scorecard (mei) 3) schedule 72h canary review (runtime-bot).
mei: will open the PR now. thanks everyone.
oscar: thanks all 1 good handoff. :thumbsup:
